solution: With $x=\\sin^{2}\\theta$, $dx=2\\sin\\theta\\cos\\theta\\,d\\theta$ and $\\sqrt{x/(1-x)}=\\tan\\theta$. Limits: $x=0\\to\\theta=0$, $x=1\\to\\theta=\\pi/2$. The integral becomes $\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}\\tan\\theta\\cdot 2\\sin\\theta\\cos\\theta\\,d\\theta=\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}2\\sin^{2}\\theta\\,d\\theta=\\int_{0}^{\\pi/2}(1-\\cos 2\\theta)\\,d\\theta=[\\theta-\\tfrac{1}{2}\\sin 2\\theta]_{0}^{\\pi/2}=\\pi/2$.
hints: Don't forget to change the limits.
